QuestionStmt.S: Which of the following is the strongest carboxylic acid?

Solution.S:
The strongest carboxylic acid is:

Option D ClCH₂COOH

Carboxylic acids become stronger when the conjugate base, the carboxylate ion RCOO⁻, is more stable.

In ClCH₂COOH, the chlorine atom is highly electronegative. It shows a strong —I effect, meaning it pulls electron density away from the —COOH group.

This helps to stabilise the carboxylate ion formed after losing H⁺:

ClCH₂COOH → ClCH₂COO⁻ + H⁺

Because the conjugate base is more stable, ClCH₂COOH releases H⁺ more easily, so it is the strongest acid.

The other acids have either hydrogen or alkyl groups near —COOH. Alkyl groups like —CH₃ and —CH₂CH₃ show +I effect, which makes the acid weaker.

So the order of acidity is approximately:

ClCH₂COOH > HCOOH > CH₃COOH > CH₃CH₂COOH

Hence, the strongest carboxylic acid is ClCH₂COOH.
